ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dumati, origin disputed. Either a loan from Proto-Germanic *dōmijaną (“to judge, think”) (whence English deem) either as a direct loan or ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewh₂- (“to smoke”), akin to Proto-Slavic *duti (“to blow, to inflate”), *dymъ (“smoke”). For the latter compare θῡμός (thūmós, “soul, emotion”), occasionally also “thought, mind”. Also compare надме́нный (nadménnyj, “supercilious, haughty, arrogant”) as another meaning change to a mental characteristic from the same root.
